To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pullout behavior and maximum equivalent bond strength of straight high-strenght steel fibers can be tailored by the matrix composition of UHPC, and that the maximum bond strength of 20 MPa was achieved in the matrix with high packing density.
the pullout behavior can be significantly influenced by the matrix composition, and that the bond strength can be increased to levels of up to 2.9 ksi.
the pullout behavior can be tailored by adjusting matrix composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of different UHPCs on the pullout behavior and the bond strength of straight high-strenght steel fibers.
the development of UHPC with high packing density and a high bond strength with high-strength straight steel fibers.
the development of UHPCs with high packing density and high physicochemical bond strength to steel fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fiber pullout bond strength is strongly influenced by the fiber/matrix interaction, which is in turn strongly dependent on the fiber/matrix packing and on the physicochemical properties of the fiber surface.
the pullout behavior is highly dependent on the fiber surface and the matrix composition.

UHPCs with a compressive strengths in the range of 190 to 200 MPa (28 ksi), and with a fine sand ratio of 50%, and a silica fume content of 20%, and a superplasticizer dosage of 2.5% of the cement content, and with the addition of hydrophobic nanoclay, provide the best conditions for a high equivalent bond strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pullout behavior can be tailored by the composition of the matrix and by the surface roughness of the embedded fiber.
a high bond strength can be achieved in UHPC with a high packing density.
the use of a high packing density of fine particles and a high compressive strength of the matrix are the main parameters for achieving a hardening bond behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bond strength of straight smooth steel fibers in UHPCs can be increased by up to 50% by optimizing matrix composition.
the pullout behavior is highly dependent on the fiber-matrix interaction.
the fiber-matrix interface is a critical parameter in UHPCs and can be manipulated by the use of different matrix compositions.
